steps.action: Step 3: open Authentication; Legal Users and Business Users start collapsed
steps.expected: Step 3 of 8; the Legal Users, Business Users and Identity providers sections are collapsed
steps.actual: Step 3 of 8: Authentication at /welcome?step=authentication in a new browser tab. aria-expanded: {"Legal Users":"false","Business Users":"false","Identity providers":"false"}. The step said "Legal Users and Business Users can use different sign-in methods."

steps.action: An old link to the Business-user portal step opens Authentication with Business Users expanded (the registry's nine-step Business-user portal step)
steps.expected: /welcome?step=portal lands on Authentication (Step 3 of 8) with Business Users expanded
steps.actual: /welcome?step=portal went to /welcome?step=authentication (Step 3 of 8: Authentication) with Business Users aria-expanded true. The section was collapsed again.

steps.action: Step 3: expand Legal Users, turn off every sign-in method, select Continue
steps.expected: OpenLaw refuses a Legal Users policy with no sign-in method: "Enable at least one sign-in method."
steps.actual: Legal Users switches at first: ["Email and password:true","Email magic link:true","Single sign-on (SSO):false:disabled","Require two-factor authentication:false"]. With both email methods off, Continue showed "Enable at least one sign-in method." and stayed at Step 3 of 8: Authentication; the saved Legal policy was unchanged ({"password":true,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false}). Both email methods were turned back on.

steps.action: Step 3: the Single sign-on (SSO) switch stays unavailable until a provider is registered; Identity providers shows Register your identity provider
steps.expected: SSO disabled with the configure tooltip; the form fields and Register provider
steps.actual: Single sign-on (SSO) was disabled; its help read "Configure an identity provider below to enable single sign-on.". Identity providers showed "Register your identity provider" with ["Display name","Provider ID","Issuer URL","Email domains","Client ID","Client secret"] and Register provider.

steps.action: Step 3: complete Register your identity provider and select Register provider; copy the callback URL; the list shows the provider; the heading changes to Add another identity provider
steps.expected: Registered notice with the callback URL on the instance address; a row with name, domains and Configured; SSO switch available
steps.actual: The step showed "Identity provider Harbor IdP is registered." and "Paste this callback URL into your IdP console: http://127.0.0.1:43385/api/auth/sso/callback". Rows: ["Harbor IdP harbor.example Configured"], with a "Remove Harbor IdP" button. The form heading now read "Add another identity provider". The Legal Users SSO switch became available. The issuer is the local OpenID Connect fixture on the lab network.

steps.action: Step 3: a second provider; each email domain can belong to one provider
steps.expected: A second row; a third registration for harbor.example is refused
steps.actual: Harbor EU IdP registered; rows ["Harbor IdP harbor.example Configured","Harbor EU IdP eu-harbor.example Configured"]. A third provider for harbor.example was refused with "harbor.example is already assigned to the identity provider Harbor IdP. Each email domain can belong to one provider.".

steps.action: Step 3: removing the last provider turns off Single sign-on (SSO) for both groups
steps.expected: With Legal SSO saved on: Remove the second provider keeps SSO; Remove the last provider turns it off and makes the switch unavailable; register the provider again
steps.actual: Continue saved Legal SSO on ({"password":true,"magicLink":true,"sso":true,"requireTwoFactor":false}) and opened Outbound email; Back returned to Authentication. Remove Harbor EU IdP left Legal SSO true. Remove Harbor IdP (the last provider) stored {"legal":false,"business":false} for SSO, the Legal switches read ["Email and password:true","Email magic link:true","Single sign-on (SSO):false:disabled","Require two-factor authentication:false"] and the form heading returned to "Register your identity provider". Harbor IdP was registered again.

steps.action: Step 5: Business Users: with no domain the switches are unavailable; an entry with an email username; Add a domain to enable the switches
steps.expected: "Add a domain to enable sign-in options."; switches unavailable; the username entry is not saved; harbor.example enables the switches
steps.actual:
With no domain the section said "Add a domain to enable sign-in options." and the switches read ["Email and password:false:disabled","Email magic link:false:disabled","Single sign-on (SSO):false:disabled","Require two-factor authentication:false:disabled"]. An entry "rowan@harbor.example" was added to the draft list; Continue stayed on Authentication with "One or more request fields are invalid. | Identity provider Harbor IdP is registered.
Paste this callback URL into your IdP console: http://127.0.0.1:43385/api/auth/sso/callback"; the saved list was []. After Add harbor.example the switches read ["Email and password:false","Email magic link:false","Single sign-on (SSO):false","Require two-factor authentication:false"].

steps.action: Step 5: while at least one domain is listed, OpenLaw refuses a Business Users policy with no sign-in method
steps.expected: Continue shows "Enable at least one sign-in method." and the Business policy is unchanged
steps.actual: With harbor.example listed and every Business method off, Continue showed "Enable at least one sign-in method." and stayed at Step 3 of 8: Authentication. Saved Business policy {"password":true,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false}; saved domains ["harbor.example"] (the list is saved before the policy).

steps.action: Step 5: removing the last domain turns off the Business sign-in methods and makes the switches unavailable; Require two-factor authentication keeps its value; adding a domain again leaves the methods off
steps.expected: Methods off and unavailable; 2FA shows on; after Add the methods are available but off
steps.actual: Before: ["Email and password:false","Email magic link:true","Single sign-on (SSO):false","Require two-factor authentication:true"]. After Remove harbor.example: ["Email and password:false:disabled","Email magic link:false:disabled","Single sign-on (SSO):false:disabled","Require two-factor authentication:true:disabled"]. After adding harbor.example again: ["Email and password:false","Email magic link:false","Single sign-on (SSO):false","Require two-factor authentication:true"]. Require two-factor authentication for Business Users was turned off again.

steps.action: Set up later on Authentication moves on without saving the step's unsaved entries; Back keeps the drafts
steps.expected: Outbound email opens; the saved domains and Business policy are unchanged; after Back the draft domain is still listed
steps.actual: Set up later opened Step 4 of 8: Outbound email. Saved state stayed {"domains":["harbor.example"],"business":{"password":true,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false}}. After Back the draft still listed unsaved.example, which was then removed.

steps.action: Steps 4 and 5: Business Users with helix.example and harbor.example and Email magic link; Legal Users with Require two-factor authentication; Continue
steps.expected: Continue saves both groups and the list, then makes the Administrator enroll
steps.actual: Continue saved Legal {"password":true,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":true} and Business {"password":false,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false} (domains read from the enrollment page: "refused until enrollment"), and opened /auth/two-factor/enroll with "Your organization requires two-factor authentication."

steps.action: Step 4: after enrollment the wizard resumes at Outbound email; your saved choices remain
steps.expected: Outbound email (Step 4 of 8); saved domains and both policies
steps.actual: A generated code turned two-factor on. Done led to /welcome?step=email: Step 4 of 8: Outbound email. Saved domains ["harbor.example","helix.example"]; Legal {"password":true,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":true}; Business {"password":false,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false}.
